'''Jordan Jerrell Sibert''' (born August 1, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]] and [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Austin Ward |title=Jordan Sibert not done with Dayton just yet |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/105002/jordan-sibert-not-done-with-dayton-just-yet |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=19 March 2015}}</ref>

==High school career==
Sibert attended [[Princeton High School (Sharonville, Ohio)|Princeton High School]] in the [[Cincinnati]] suburb of [[Sharonville, Ohio]]. As a junior, he averaged 13.3 points per game. He improved his scoring to an 18.7 points per game clip as a senior while leading the team to a 19–5 and a berth in the regional semifinals. Sibert was named the Ohio's Gatorade Player of the Year and the [[Associated Press]] selected him to the First Team All-Ohio. Ranked seventh best shooting guard in 2010 by [[Rivals.com]],<ref>{{cite news |author1=Doug Harris |title=UD in hunt for Sibert |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98168721/ud-in-hunt-for-sibert/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=10 April 2012 |page=C1|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> Sibert committed to [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].<ref name=Dayton>{{cite news|url=http://www.daytonflyers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=10|title=#24 Jordan Sibert|work=[[Dayton Flyers]]|accessdate=September 25, 2015}}</ref>

==College career==
Sibert averaged 11.4 minutes, 3.0 points and 1.4 rebounds as a sophomore on Ohio State's Final Four team in 2011–12.<ref name=Dayton/> Sibert saw his minutes decrease as the season went on. He opted to transfer to the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Two players leaving Ohio State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7821509/jd-weatherspoon-jordan-sibert-leaving-ohio-state-buckeyes-program |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=16 April 2012}}</ref> after the season due to lack of playing time, having remained on the bench in the NCAA tournament.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Lemerises|first1=Doug|title=Where is Ohio State's shooting? It transferred to Dayton|url=http://www.cleveland.com/osu/index.ssf/2014/01/where_is_ohio_states_shooting.html|accessdate=September 25, 2015|newspaper=[[The Plain Dealer]]|date=January 17, 2014}}</ref> OSU coach [[Thad Matta]] blamed poor shooting and subpar defense for Sibert not receiving the minutes he wanted.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wasserman|first1=Ari|title="This is what I left Ohio State for": Dayton's Jordan Sibert embraces spotlight while trying to take down former team|url=http://www.cleveland.com/osu/index.ssf/2014/03/jordan_sibert_dayton_flyers_oh.html|accessdate=September 28, 2015|work=[[The Plain Dealer]]|date=March 20, 2014}}</ref>

As a junior, Sibert led Dayton in scoring at 12.2 points per game, shooting 42.6% from behind the arc. He scored in double-figures 24 times and led Dayton to an Elite Eight appearance in the NCAA Tournament.<ref name=Dayton/> He scored 18 points in defeating [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] 82–72 in the Sweet 16.<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 11 seed Dayton reaches Elite 8 for first time since 1984|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400548862|access-date=September 28, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 28, 2014}}</ref>

As a senior with the Flyers, Sibert averaged 16.1 points, 3.3 rebounds, two assists and 1.7 steals per game.<ref name=Magic>{{cite news|last1=Highkin|first1=Sean|title=Report: Magic add undrafted Dayton guard Jordan Sibert to training-camp roster|url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2015/08/29/report-magic-add-undrafted-dayton-guard-jordan-sibert-to-training-camp-roster/|accessdate=September 25, 2015|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=August 29, 2015}}</ref> He was named to the First Team All-Atlantic 10.<ref>{{cite web|title=2014–15 Atlantic 10 Men's Basketball Awards|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/pdf9/3272408.pdf|website=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|accessdate=September 25, 2015}}</ref> With a 25–8 record, Dayton was the last team selected to the NCAA Tournament. "It's just a blessing to have an opportunity to play in the tournament," Sibert said. "Some guys didn't hear their name called at all."<ref name=nyt>{{cite news|last1=Maks|first1=Patrick|title=Dayton Relishes Role as a Longtime Tournament Host|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/03/19/sports/ncaabasketball/dayton-relishes-role-as-a-longtime-tournament-host.html?_r=0|accessdate=September 28, 2015|work=[[New York Times]]|date=March 18, 2015}}</ref> He led Dayton to a Sweet 16 appearance and finished his Dayton career with 1,030 points. Despite playing only two years, his 163 three-pointers rank seventh in Dayton history.<ref name=Dayton/>

==Professional career==
[[File:Jordan Sibert.jpg|thumb|left|Sibert playing for the College Park Skyhawks in 2019]]
After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Sibert joined the [[Orlando Magic]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League|Orlando Summer League]] where he saw action in all three games, averaging 11.3 points, three rebounds and 1.7 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Jablonski|first1=David|title=Dayton Flyers' Sibert going to training camp with Magic|url=http://www.daytondailynews.com/news/sports/college-basketball/dayton-flyers-sibert-going-to-training-camp-with-m/nnStd/|accessdate=September 25, 2015|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=August 28, 2015}}</ref> On September 24, 2015, he signed with the Magic,<ref name=Magic/><ref>{{cite news|title=Magic Sign Four Free Agents To Round Out Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-four-free-agents-round-out-training-camp-roster|accessdate=September 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2015}}</ref> only to be waived by the team on October 19 after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Magic Waive Appling and Sibert|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-appling-and-sibert|accessdate=October 19, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2015}}</ref> On October 31, he was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Magic.<ref>{{cite news|title=Erie BayHawks Announce Affiliate, Returning Players|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065433|accessdate=October 31, 2015|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 31, 2015}}</ref>

On July 19, 2016, Sibert signed with the Greek team [[P.A.O.K. BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jordan Sibert inks with PAOK Thessaloniki|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/206806/jordan-sibert-inks-with-paok-thessaloniki.html|work=Sportando.com|date=July 20, 2016|accessdate=July 20, 2016}}</ref>

On August 23, 2017, Sibert was selected by the new incarnation of the [[Erie BayHawks (2017–)|Erie BayHawks]] in the NBA G League expansion draft. On August 29, he opted to sign with the German club [[Mitteldeutscher BC]] instead.<ref>{{cite web | title = MBC verstärkt Kader – Thomas und Zazai verlassen die Wölfe | work = [[Mitteldeutscher BC]] | date = August 29, 2017 | url = http://www.mitteldeutscherbc.de/mbcnews.php#1633 | accessdate = August 31, 2017 | language = German | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20130622154353/http://www.mitteldeutscherbc.de/mbcnews.php#1633 | archivedate = June 22, 2013 }}</ref> Sibert averaged 12.2 points and 2.6 rebounds with [[Mitteldeutscher BC]]. In March 2018, he signed with the [[Skyliners Frankfurt]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FRAPORT SKYLINERS verpflichten Jordan Sibert |url=https://www.fraport-skyliners.de/news/artikel/datum/2018/03/16/fraport-skyliners-verpflichten-jordan-sibert/ |website=[[Skyliners Frankfurt]] |accessdate=September 14, 2018 |language=German}}</ref>

In October 2018, Sibert was added to the training camp roster of the Erie BayHawks.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hartman |first1=Billy |title=Erie BayHawks Finalize 2018 Training Camp Roster |url=https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/erie-bayhawks-finalize-2018-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |accessdate=November 3, 2018 |date=October 20, 2018 |archive-date=November 3, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103211026/https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/erie-bayhawks-finalize-2018-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On February 20, 2019, Sibert signed a 10-day contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Jordan Sibert to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-sign-jordan-sibert-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|accessdate=February 20, 2019|date=February 20, 2019}}</ref> Sibert was reacquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2017–)|Erie BayHawks]] on March{{nbsp}}3 after the conclusion of the 10-day contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jordan Sibert Rejoins Erie|url=https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/jordan-sibert-rejoins-erie/|date=March 3, 2019|work=NBA.com|accessdate=March 3, 2019}}</ref> On October 8, 2019, Sibert re-joined the Hawks for training camp.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Jordan Sibert|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-jordan-sibert|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 9, 2019|date=October 8, 2019}}</ref>

On October 18, 2019, the Hawks waived Sibert.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-brooks-derrickson-mccall-and-sibert|title = Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers on Brooks, Derrickson, McCall and Sibert|website = [[NBA.com]]}}</ref> He was then added to the roster of the [[College Park Skyhawks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=College Park Skyhawks Announce Training Camp Roster |url=https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/news/college-park-skyhawks-announce-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |accessdate=November 17, 2019 |date=October 29, 2019 |archive-date=November 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191117202538/https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/news/college-park-skyhawks-announce-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 12, 2020, Sibert scored 35 points in a 123–119 victory over [[Raptors 905]], the Skyhawks' fourth straight win.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Goodman |first1=Darius |title=Jordan Sibert drops 35 enroute to College Park Skyhawks' fourth straight win |url=https://www.henryherald.com/sports/jordan-sibert-drops-35-enroute-to-college-park-skyhawks-fourth-straight-win/article_8d015d0a-3570-11ea-8cb5-fbdd23d7b32e.html |accessdate=June 21, 2020 |work=[[Henry Herald]] |date=January 12, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 13.9 points per game for the Skyhawks.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jablonski |first1=David |title=Former Flyer Sibert to play for Team USA in FIBA AmeriCup qualifying |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/former-flyer-sibert-to-play-for-team-usa-in-fiba-americup-qualifying/SKGIYUGCTJDGHJ4SJBDN2EZUYM/ |access-date=November 7, 2021 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=February 2, 2021}}</ref>

On February 24, 2022, Sibert was traded to the [[Wisconsin Herd]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 24, 2022|access-date=February 24, 2022}}</ref>

On November 28, 2022, Sibert returned to Greece for [[P.A.O.K. BC|PAOK]], signing for the rest of the season in order to replace the injured [[Zaccheus Darko-Kelly]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.paokbc.gr/el/nea/omadas/2053-o-jordan-sibert-mateco|website=paokbc.gr|title=O Jordan Sibert επιστρέφει στον ΠΑΟΚ mateco|date=November 28, 2022|access-date=November 29, 2022}}</ref> In 21 league games, he averaged 6.2 points and 1.7 rebounds, playing around 14 minutes per contest.

On August 17, 2023, Sibert moved to another Greek club, signing with [[ASK Karditsas B.C.|Karditsa]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jordan Sibert joins Karditsas |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/824592/Jordan-Sibert-joins-Karditsas |access-date=2023-08-18 |website=www.eurobasket.com}}</ref>
